title: Undoing a Bad Commit Safely
description: Safely undo a breaking commit on shared main without rewriting history.
objective: Safely reverse the breaking change on shared main while preserving the original commit in history and restoring the application to its previous working state.
whatToDo: Keep the original commit in history.
hints: Inspect the recent commit history and the changes introduced by the latest commit. Identify which commit caused the problem.
Because main is shared, the original commit should remain in history. Think about the Git operation designed to reverse a commit while preserving its history.
After reversing the change, verify that the original commit is still in main's history and that the application has returned to its previous working state.

intro.message: The latest commit broke the build, and everyone has already pulled main. We need to undo the change without rewriting shared history.

revertBadCommit.message: Good. The breaking change has been reversed with a new commit. Now make sure the original history is still intact and the working state is clean.

verifyRecovery.message: Exactly. The original commit is still in history, the change was safely reversed, and main is back to the working state.

success.message: Build's green again and nobody has to force-pull anything. Exactly the right call.

failure.message: The solution isn't quite right yet. Keep the original commit in history and use a new commit to reverse its changes.
